title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator. Each pair used one shared initial LLM generation and compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate; (b) guarded — run deterministic validation and permit at most one automated constrained repair. Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.99667) and guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and the ≤1‑repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue to one hard sequencing omission that the constrained repair fixed.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for NetOps tasks including natural‑language intent → device configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment changes, semantic correctness properties (sequencing constraints, reachability, policy preservation) are operationally critical and typically require deterministic checks beyond syntactic validation. A common engineering pattern is generate→validate→repair: pair a generative model with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair to reduce operational risk. The measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends fundamentally on what is held fixed (the estimand), the single‑shot quality of the generator, validator expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

This paper reports a preregistered paired experiment (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue attributable to a verifier+bounded repair applied to the same LLM output. For each intent we produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (gpt-5-mini) reused across conditions, and compared accepting that candidate as‑is (baseline) versus running a deterministic validator and allowing at most one constrained repair (guarded). The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier and a single constrained repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that same candidate without repair? Our contribution is an artifact‑archived, preregistered paired evaluation that (i) quantifies deterministic rescue under tight model‑call budgets, (ii) provides per‑episode validator traces and the single repair transcript for forensic inspection, and (iii) interprets ceiling effects and estimand conditioning for NetOps deployment policies.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document widespread activity applying LLMs to NetOps tasks and highlight tool‑augmentation strategies that allow LLMs to call validators or simulators to coordinate multi‑step workflows [1,2,3]. Empirical reports show that integrating deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness over unconstrained generation, but the magnitude depends on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,4,5]. Planner‑centric and ReAct‑style frameworks demonstrate richer tool orchestration but conflate benefits from multi‑step tool use with benefits from repeated model draws [2,6]. Work on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets proposes entropy‑ or consistency‑based detectors and retrieval/self‑reflection mitigations; their effectiveness depends on threat models and validator semantics [6]. Hybrid approaches that combine formal fault localization or symbolic verification with generative repair operators report variable success depending on fault class and verifier expressiveness [7,8]. Our study explicitly isolates deterministic rescue by conditioning on a single LLM draw, thereby bounding the verifier/repair effect from resampling benefits emphasized in related work.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The confirmatory design and analysis plan were preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory executor and multiplicity plan were fixed before observing main‑run outcomes. The preregistration SHA‑256 is archived and associated with the study id.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were deterministically generated into a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership and ensured 100 pairs per stratum in the confirmatory run. (Note: the optional calibration pilot described in the preregistration was not executed; that omission is reported and accounted for in the interpretation.)

Shared_initial protocol, generator, and validator. To measure only deterministic rescue we implemented a shared_initial protocol: for each pair the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate reused verbatim for baseline and guarded conditions. The generator used was gpt-5-mini; the guarded pipeline used a deterministic semantic validator that enforces sequencing, required_command_count, state preservation, topology reachability invariants, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand.

Repair operator, contamination controls, and exclusion rules. The guarded pipeline permits at most one automated constrained repair per pair, limited to localized sequencing/insert edits (e.g., inserting a missing 'admin down' step). Repair attempts are deterministically re‑validated; candidates remaining flagged after the single permitted edit count as failures for guarded in the primary analysis. Contamination detection included negative controls and automated invariant checks; pairs were excluded from the confirmatory analysis only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/infrastructure outage. All provider failures, exclusions, and contamination flags were logged and archived.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The preregistered adapter completed the run with 600 completed episodes (300 pairs). Model call accounting: 301 model calls were used (one shared_initial per pair plus one repair invocation across the run). No dual‑call provider outages or excluded pairs occurred; deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring returned baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.996667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts (n10,n01) returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) is 0.0033333. A paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval (seed = 1729, B = 10000) yields [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance m = n10 + n01 = 1 is minimal, exact inference has limited sensitivity and the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible improvement to at most one percentage point under these conditions.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per stratum: low baseline 100/100, guarded 100/100; medium baseline 100/100, guarded 100/100; high baseline 99/100, guarded 100/100. The single discordant pair occurred in the high stratum and invoked the allowed automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a required 'admin down' prior to VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator then reported a pass; this single deterministic rescue consumed the only repair invocation recorded across the 300 pairs. Contamination and negative controls did not produce unexpected passes; missingness summaries show zero failed or unscorable episodes.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational meaning. The shared_initial estimand corresponds to operational policies that tightly budget model calls (cost, latency, or governance) and therefore measures only deterministic rescue applied to an identical candidate. Pipelines that permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration evaluate a different estimand and typically achieve higher success rates by exploiting generator variance; those workflows must be assessed with their own preregistered designs.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. Baseline single‑shot performance was near ceiling (299/300) under this synthetic suite, producing minimal discordance and limiting power to detect small absolute improvements. This outcome illustrates the value of small calibration pilots for estimating discordance when generator performance may approach ceiling; the preregistration included such a pilot but it was not executed.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The lone observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL semantics) were not prevalent in this suite. The guard's marginal utility therefore hinges on the real‑world distribution of failure modes and on validator expressiveness. Richer validators that capture reachability or higher‑order invariants would likely increase observable rescue rates, at the cost of more complex validator engineering.

Repair budget tradeoffs and operational implications. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to quantify bounded deterministic rescue. Iterative repair, broader edit operators, or verifier‑guided regeneration would increase rescue opportunities but correspond to a different operational policy and estimand. In this run the guarded pipeline produced a deterministic rescue with minimal additional model‑call cost (1 extra call across 300 pairs), suggesting that, where localized sequencing omissions are a dominant failure mode and model calls are budgeted, a bounded repair policy can offer low marginal cost benefit.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired comparison that conditions on a single shared_initial LLM draw per intent, a deterministic verifier plus a single constrained repair produced a single deterministic rescue out of 300 pairs: baseline 299/300 and guarded 300/300, absolute paired difference 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00, 0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limits inferential sensitivity under this synthetic suite and repair budget. Our archived artifacts (preregistration, task manifests, per‑episode validator traces, repair trace, and analysis inputs) permit replay and targeted follow‑on studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distribution, or repair budget to assess the practical impact of guarded pipelines under alternative operational policies.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: the run evaluated only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator; results may not generalize to other LLMs, validators, or richer edit operators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot omitted: the preregistered optional pilot for discordance estimation and power calibration was not executed; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was made.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated constrained repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
